claims.title: Exact rational vertex reduction for finite prior polytopes
claims.scope: nonempty compact rational subsets of a finite probability simplex represented by linear inequalities
assumptions: the ambiguity set is U={q in simplex:Aq<=b} with rational A and b
the simplex equality is eliminated exactly
every active basis below the configured cap is exhausted
nonclaims: active-basis enumeration is not a polynomial-time large-instance guarantee
an ambiguity polytope is not automatically a statistical confidence set

claims.title: Continuous polyhedral minimax regret reduces to ambiguity vertices
claims.scope: finite one-shot zero-error binary-prefix codebooks and a compact rational prior polytope
assumptions: the law-specific oracle is L*(q)=min_d q dot ell_d over the declared deterministic code universe
regret is measured in expected binary-prefix length
the ambiguity set is convex and compact
nonclaims: the theorem does not identify minimax absolute loss with minimax regret
the result is one-shot and does not establish an asymptotic graph-entropy theorem

claims.title: Shared-randomness polyhedral length and regret games are finite vertex games
claims.scope: source-independent shared codebook randomness against a compact rational prior polytope
assumptions: the source law is chosen independently of the realized shared codebook seed
all decoders know the realized codebook
the deterministic bounded code universe is complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the exact random-bit cost of sampling a codebook mixture is not priced
private encoder randomness is not substituted for common randomness

claims.title: Huber contamination is an exact rational simplex polytope
claims.scope: finite rational nominal source laws and rational contamination fraction in [0,1]
assumptions: q=(1-epsilon)p+epsilon r with r an arbitrary probability vector
nonclaims: Huber contamination is not identical to a same-radius TV ball
epsilon is a model parameter unless separately calibrated from data

claims.title: Finite-sample multinomial TV confidence radius from L1 concentration
claims.scope: i.i.d. samples from one stationary categorical law on a fixed finite alphabet
assumptions: the Weissman-Ordentlich-Seroussi-Verdu-Weinberger finite-sample L1 inequality applies
the alphabet is fixed before sampling
samples are independent and identically distributed
nonclaims: the confidence guarantee does not cover arbitrary dependence, drift, adaptive censoring, or covariate shift
the transcendental radius calculation is numerically evaluated and outward-rounded rather than labeled exact rational arithmetic

claims.title: Data-calibrated robust code gives a high-probability expected-length upper bound
claims.scope: the selected deterministic TV-robust prefix code under the i.i.d. categorical sampling model
assumptions: the confidence event that the true source law lies in the calibrated TV ball holds
the exact TV robust code certificate is valid for the outward-rounded rational radius
nonclaims: the result is an upper confidence guarantee for expected one-shot code length, not evidence for a simulator
coverage is inherited from the stated sampling model rather than from robust optimization itself

claims.title: Complete-confusion i.i.d. block prefix redundancy vanishes as at most one bit per block
claims.scope: positive-support finite i.i.d. sources whose every source symbol is mutually confusable and therefore requires a distinct zero-error message
assumptions: block sequence probabilities are the exact product law
binary Huffman coding is applied to complete block messages
the source has positive support for the strict upper entropy inequality
nonclaims: the theorem is not generalized to arbitrary confusion graphs without specifying the multi-letter graph product
amortized source-coding rate is not queueing delay, peak bandwidth, or parent-substrate resource cost

claims.title: Symmetric K3 interval ambiguity separates deterministic and shared minimax values
assumptions: binary-prefix zero-error coding
shared codebook seed is source independent
nonclaims: the numerical values are specific to the declared ambiguity set

claims.title: Bounded exact polyhedral ambiguity, regret, calibration, and block-coding audit
claims.scope: the bounded rational and finite numerical instances exercised by the repository test suite
assumptions: all configured active-basis, code-universe, game, and block-sequence caps complete without truncation
the statistical transcendental calculation uses the declared Decimal precision and outward rational rounding
nonclaims: bounded test agreement is not a scalability theorem
CI success does not upgrade a finite check into a physical claim
